Imagine aliens came to earth and began to eat all our food until there was nothing left for us. That is how invasive species thrive, by intruding in an environment that is not theirs and taking over leaving native species to decline in numbers. The invasive species benefit at the native species' expense. Although some may argue that scientists [crossed out: that] in this field of study are bias, this does not make the information regarding the dangers of invasive species false. Invasive species should be controlled because the invaders prey on native species and their population declines. This can lead to endangerment or even extinction of a native species. a predator to the native population changes how diverse the particular environment is, in this case and island, and how this affects the native population in a very negative way.

Another example that supports the need to control invasive species is how the effects of the [crossed out: nat] invasive species affect humans when they try to prevent it. The decrease in native population, spread of pathogens, and effects on the environment cause people to have to step in. Doing so affects the economy greatly, as stated by Daniel Simberloff and Marcel Rejmánek, “the cost of biological invasions to the economy of the United States alone is estimated at over $100 billion [crossed out: illegible annually] annually” (Source 3, lines 22–23). Not only does these invasive species affect [crossed out: animals] other native species [crossed out: and] of plants and animals, but humans are also paying the price; quite literally speaking because of [crossed out: the] how expensive it is to control the invasive species.

[crossed out: Some] However, others argue that scientists aren't looking at the full picture of the study, and are only focusing on the negative effects. According to some, not all invasive species are bad but most scientists and researchers prefer to put their time into studying and preventing invasive species that cause harm. As stated by Fred Pearce, “The charge is that invasion biologists have shown systematic bias in their studies. They have started from the presumption that alien species are

bad and sought out research topics to confirm their view” (Source 4, lines 14–16). This exemplifies the view that scientists are bias and only assume that all invasive species are bad and seek to prove it with [crossed out: spe] evidence. Although this may be true, the evidence [crossed out: they found] the scientists have found regarding [crossed out: the] invasive species have proved the extent of their negative effects. The [crossed out: species] invaders not only prey on native populations but also decrease their population by destroying the native species' habitat as well as the plant species within [crossed out: that] that environment. As shown by Asher Elbein, “Insects like the emerald ash borer and fungi like chesnut blight have devastated American [crossed out: forests] forests” (Source 1 lines 29–30). This text [crossed out: exe helps ex] explains how [crossed out: there are many] destructive as well as deadly invasive species are. Despite the fact that some believe scientists are bias, this is probably because there is more evidence that goes against invasive species than supports it.

information collected on these negative effects are still true. Invasive species affect the whole world especially after the introduction of mass transportation and more rapid transportation. This is still a problem in the world and needs to be controlled.
